Programme-specific entry requirements for postgraduate applicants with international qualifications
The minimum entry requirements for applicants to specific postgraduate degree programmes are listed below. These requirements are intended as a guide only and you may need to obtain a higher average grade than the one listed in the table below, dependent on previous study undertaken. Please note that not all postgraduate programmes are listed. Most postgraduate programmes at the University of Canterbury require you to have completed an undergraduate degree at a recognised
university (or similar) in a field relevant to your chosen specialisation. If you are applying for a 120 point Master’s degree, by thesis only, you must have completed a year of postgraduate study, following an undergraduate degree. Your grades in specific courses you have taken in this field can affect entry to a postgraduate programme.
In addition to the minimum University admission requirements, you must fulfil additional entry requirements to gain entry to most postgraduate programmes. These additional requirements vary depending on the programme and specialisation that you are applying for. Please refer to the Postgraduate Prospectus or contact the appropriate School or Faculty for more information.
If you are interested in doctoral study, please see Doctoral entry requirements (https://www.canterbury.ac.nz/study/getting-started/admission-and-enrolment/enrol-doctoral-degree)
For UC Online programmes and entry requirements, please visit: https://uconline.ac.nz/courses
